pages.text: Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper, gave them a big piece of cheese. "Cheese! I want lots!" Pongi hopped. Mom, wearing her headscarf, put it on the shelf. "Just one piece for a snack."
At snack time, Mom cut a piece of cheese and put it on a plate. Pongi ate it, then looked at the cheese on the shelf. "I want just one more piece..." She wandered beneath the shelf.
Mom went out to fetch water. Pongi stretched a paw up to the shelf and gobbled the cheese. "Just one more piece, just one more..." The cheese got smaller and smaller.
It was evening. Fish was on the table. But Pongi's tummy was full of cheese and felt firm. "I'm full... I can't eat fish." She put both paws on her tummy.
Mom gently rubbed Pongi's tummy. "You ate so much cheese that there's no room for fish." "But I want some..." she said quietly. "I'll show you how to eat just one piece," said Mom.
"Your tummy is a little room," said Mom. "If it's full of cheese, the fish can't come in." In Mom's story, a fish bounced outside the door. "I need to leave room!" Pongi nodded.
Mom cut one piece of cheese and put the rest up on the shelf. She sang, "Just one piece of cheese! Leave room for fish." Pongi copied her. "Just one piece of cheese!"

At snack time the next day, Mom put one piece on a plate. Pongi ate it and set the empty plate firmly on the table with both paws. She didn't look at the shelf! She thumped her tail. "Just one piece of cheese!"
It was evening. Her tummy rumbled! Pongi ate the fish. "Was it always this tasty?" She sang, "One, just one piece of cheese! Two, the rest on the shelf! Three, meals come first!"
Mom hugged Pongi. "You waited without looking at the shelf!" With just one piece of cheese, the fish at dinner tastes much better. Pongi called, "Just one piece of cheese!"
